title: Ezekiel 25:1–7
context: The LORD’s word comes to Ezekiel, who is addressed as “son of man” and told to set his face toward the children of Ammon and prophesy against them. The Lord GOD’s charge is their cry of “Aha!” against his sanctuary when it was profaned, against the land of Israel when it was made desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into captivity. Because of that cry, they will be delivered to the children of the east for a possession; those peoples will camp in the land, eat the fruit, and drink the milk. Rabbah will become a stable for camels, and Ammon a resting place for flocks, and they will know that he is the LORD. A second word names the clapping of hands, the stamping of feet, and the rejoicing with all the contempt of their soul against the land of Israel. The LORD has stretched out his hand; they will be plundered, cut off from the peoples, and destroyed, and they will know that he is the LORD. The children of the east are often taken as desert peoples to Ammon’s east; the oracle does not name them further. Rabbah is named as Ammon’s city, the place that will become a stable; later identifications of the site are more than the verse itself supplies.

verses.text: The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
verses.arminianNotes:
“The LORD’s word came to me, saying,” The new unit opens as the earlier ones do: the word comes to the prophet. The oracles that follow are the LORD’s speech against neighboring peoples, beginning with Ammon.

Arminian readers take the heading as a fresh word, a real address now turned outward from Judah to a neighbor who has rejoiced at Judah’s fall.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers hear the same heading as the LORD’s initiative, the source of all that will be said against Ammon and, later, against Moab, Edom, and the Philistines.

Shared ground: the speaker of the oracles is the LORD, and the word comes to Ezekiel. The traditions begin together.

verses.text: “Son of man, set your face toward the children of Ammon, and prophesy against them.
verses.arminianNotes:
“Son of man, set your face toward the children of Ammon, and prophesy against them.” The prophet is again “son of man,” and he is to set his face toward Ammon and prophesy against them. The gesture is a directed word, faced toward the people named.

Arminian readers hear a real turning of the prophet’s face, a word aimed at Ammon as hearers of a charge, not only as a subject of distant comment.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the same title, the same setting of the face, and the same command to prophesy against the children of Ammon as the LORD’s sending.

Shared ground: the first neighbor named is Ammon, and the prophet is sent against them. The title remains the ordinary address of the book.

verses.text: Tell the children of Ammon, ‘Hear the word of the Lord GOD! The Lord GOD says, “Because you said, ‘Aha!’ against my sanctuary when it was profaned, and against the land of Israel when it was made desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into captivity,
verses.arminianNotes:
Ammon is told to hear the word of the Lord GOD, “Because you said, ‘Aha!’ against my sanctuary when it was profaned, and against the land of Israel when it was made desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into captivity,” The offense is a cry of “Aha!” over three wounds: the sanctuary profaned, the land desolate, the house of Judah gone into captivity. The taunt is the ground of the oracle, a rejoicing over Israel’s ruin, and it is told in those three clauses without added color.

Arminian readers hear a neighbor’s glad cry over holy things defiled and a people led away, a contempt the LORD takes as a reason for judgment, and a word Ammon can recognize as about their own mouth.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the same “Aha!” against sanctuary, land, and house of Judah as the Lord GOD’s stated reason, the taunt that calls forth the sentence that follows.

Shared ground: the cry of “Aha!” is the charge. The three losses they celebrated are the sanctuary, the land, and the captivity.

verses.text: therefore, behold, I will deliver you to the children of the east for a possession. They will set their encampments in you and make their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruit and they will drink your milk.
verses.arminianNotes:
“therefore, behold, I will deliver you to the children of the east for a possession. They will set their encampments in you and make their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruit and they will drink your milk.” The children of the east will take Ammon as a possession, camp and dwell there, and live off the fruit and the milk. Many readers take those easterners as desert peoples on Ammon’s east; the verse names them only as “the children of the east”.

Arminian readers hear a reversal: the people who rejoiced at Judah’s loss will themselves be occupied and eaten up, a judgment they can still hear as the LORD’s answer to their “Aha!”
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the same delivery to the children of the east, the encampments and dwellings, and the eating of fruit and drinking of milk, as the LORD’s appointed possession of Ammon.

Shared ground: Ammon becomes a possession, and the east will live off the land. The identity of those peoples is left as the verse states it.

verses.text: I will make Rabbah a stable for camels and the children of Ammon a resting place for flocks. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.arminianNotes:
“I will make Rabbah a stable for camels and the children of Ammon a resting place for flocks. Then you will know that I am the LORD.” Rabbah, named as the city, will be a stable for camels; the people will be a resting place for flocks. The end of the word is knowledge: they will know that he is the LORD. Rabbah is Ammon’s city in the oracle; later geography of the site is not supplied in the line itself.

Arminian readers hear a capital turned to a camel-yard, and a people turned to pasture, a humbling whose purpose is that they know the LORD, a knowledge still held out as the outcome of the judgment.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the same making of Rabbah into a stable and of Ammon into a resting place for flocks, and the same “Then you will know that I am the LORD.” as his own purpose in the sentence.

Shared ground: Rabbah and Ammon are brought low, and they will know that he is the LORD. The formula is the book’s familiar close.

verses.text: For the Lord GOD says: “Because you have clapped your hands, stamped with the feet, and rejoiced with all the contempt of your soul against the land of Israel,
verses.arminianNotes:
“Because you have clapped your hands, stamped with the feet, and rejoiced with all the contempt of your soul against the land of Israel,” A second because is given: the clapping, the stamping, and the rejoicing, with all the contempt of their soul, against the land of Israel. The body of the taunt is in view—hands, feet, and soul—and the object is the land itself.

Arminian readers hear a full-hearted contempt, not a passing remark, a joy over Israel’s land that the LORD treats as guilt, and a charge that still names their own gestures.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the clapping, the stamping, and the rejoicing with all the contempt of the soul against the land of Israel as the Lord GOD’s further ground of judgment.

Shared ground: the contempt is open and bodily, and it is against the land of Israel. The two “because” clauses of the unit stand together.

verses.text: therefore, behold, I have stretched out my hand on you, and will deliver you for a plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples, and I will cause you to perish out of the countries. I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.arminianNotes:
“therefore, behold, I have stretched out my hand on you, and will deliver you for a plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples, and I will cause you to perish out of the countries. I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.” The stretched-out hand means plunder, being cut off from the peoples, perishing out of the countries, and destruction. Once more, they will know that he is the LORD. The four verbs of ruin are the LORD’s, and the knowledge of the LORD is again the end.

Arminian readers hear a hand already stretched out, a future of plunder and destruction that answers the contempt, and a purpose that they know the LORD, a purpose the judgment itself will serve.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers take the stretched-out hand, the plunder, the cutting off, the perishing, the destruction, and the knowledge that he is the LORD as his own settled word against Ammon.

Shared ground: the hand is stretched out, and they will know that he is the LORD. The unit against Ammon closes on that knowledge.
